plate.narration: A mule has sat down in the middle of the north road. It is chewing a daisy. Its owner pleads, the wagons grumble, and the sack on its back hums away. Nobody is going anywhere just yet.

objectives.label: Noticed the silence follows the stones
Sang a route-song verse at the relay

goal.text: Follow the rush up the north road and find out what the road remembers.

steps.label: Find a safe place to camp

facet_depot.name: The Depot Stone
facet_depot.text: Its depot tag still says 'Strongbox 9. SOLD.' It rings like a dinner bell.

verses_relay_spiral.name: The Spiral Verses
verses_relay_spiral.text: New route-song verses on bark. Sung in order, the roads curl around the gemfalls.

scene_north_roads.narration: Follow the rush up the north road and find out what the road remembers. Upbound wagons carry picks. Downbound wagons carry tired people. Up ahead is the big gem depot, where the rush stores its stones.

scene_north_roads_fall_in.narration: You fall in between a wagon of picks and a wagon of pickles. The pickle seller offers you one on a stick. It is bigger than the stick.

scene_drovers_wagon.narration: The lead drover from the ford spots you. "Mudlarks! Up you get!" he booms. It is what he calls everybody he likes. You ride the tailboard with your legs dangling, eating dried apples.

scene_out_of_marsh.narration: You climb out of the marsh with mud to your knees and the boggarts' hum in your ears. Nobody has a seat for you, so you carry water for a wagon that smells of turnips.

scene_jackalope_race.narration: Jackalopes, little antlered hares, race the wagons for fun. One thumps beside you and points its nose at a mile marker. It wants a race.

check_jackalope_race.prompt: Race a jackalope to the mile marker

onSuccess.narration: You run like the wind and lose by one ear, which is the best anybody has done all season. The jackalope looks you over with new respect and thumps once. That means friends. It lopes along beside you for the next mile, showing off.

onFailure.narration: You run like the wind. The jackalope runs like a much faster wind, then sits at the mile marker cleaning its antlers until you catch up. It thumps once anyway, as if to say: nice try. Then it is off to race a cart.

scene_jackalope_race_cheer.narration: You cheer for the horses. The jackalope wins by a mile, turns around, and races them back. The horses decline to discuss it.

scene_jackalope_race_fly.narration: Your griffin races it from above. The jackalope zigzags and dives under a wagon. Nobody wins, which by jackalope rules makes you best friends. It lopes along under your shadow, thumping happily.

scene_empty_stretch.narration: Then comes a whole mile with no jackalopes. Not one thump. Even the birds have gone quiet. Where did they all stop, and why?

scene_empty_stretch_racer.narration: Your jackalope friend stops dead at one stone. It thumps three times and won't come closer to you. It is not the road it is worried about. It is what you are carrying.

scene_empty_stretch_keep_walking.narration: No thumps. No antlers. Even the birds whisper. You walk on to the downbound lane without finding where the silence began.

check_jackalopes.prompt: Count the jackalopes and find where they stop

onSuccess.narration: You count forty-one, forty-two, forty-three, and then none. Not one. The last jackalope sits exactly at the edge of the silence like the period at the end of a sentence, and you can draw the line from where you stand.

onFailure.narration: You get to forty-one jackalopes, and then one of them sits up and stares at you until you lose count. It has won. You do not know what, but it has definitely won.

scene_silence_follows.narration: You notice it all at once. The warrens go quiet around the depot, around the gem wagons, and around YOU. Every jackalope near a stone has gone underground. The land is not flinching from the eruption. It is flinching from the stones.

scene_downbound.narration: A prospector called Ma Ruddle watches her wagon being auctioned. "Never mind the wagon. I've lost my nephew Tib! Small. Orange hat. Talks to horses." Find him, and she will give you her depot papers.

scene_downbound_fly_look.narration: From above, the crowd is a river of brown and gray hats. Except one. An orange dot stands perfectly still beside a pony, talking.

scene_downbound_work_crowd.narration: Your kitsune climbs onto a crate and booms, "LOST! ONE SMALL BOY! ORANGE HAT! TALKS TO HORSES!" The whole lane stops to listen. Then forty people point the same way.

check_relay.narration: Ma Ruddle can't shout over the auction. A centaur relay runner skids up. "Small boy, orange hat, talks to horses? Hand me the word. I'll pass it down the line."

interaction.cue: Catch the message, then pass it on down the line.
interaction.objectLabel: The word: small boy, orange hat

onSuccess.narration: The word goes runner to runner, faster than you can eat a honeycake. Then it comes back: found!

onFailure.narration: "Small orange horse," says one runner, and gallops off. Luckily the next runner has met Tib. Word comes back: found!

check_search.narration: There! An orange hat bobs above the crowd, then ducks behind one of three wagons. "Watch which one he hides behind," says Ma Ruddle, wringing her hands.

interaction.cue: Watch the orange hat duck between the wagons, then pick the wagon it hides behind.

onSuccess.narration: You spot the hat, lose it, spot it again, and find Tib explaining something very seriously to a pony.

onFailure.narration: Every wagon hides a pumpkin in a hat. Later the relay finds Tib, but Ma Ruddle's papers have gone in the auction pile.

onAssisted.narration: A kind carter points the way. You find Tib explaining something to a pony.

scene_tib_found.narration: There is Tib, chatting with a pony. Ma Ruddle hugs him, then gives you a honeycake and a folded bill of sale. "For the stone I left at the depot," she says. "I'm going home. You have it."

scene_stubborn_mule.narration: A mule blocks the downbound lane, calmly chewing a daisy. Its owner pleads. The wagons shout. On its back, a gem sack hums. How will you get it moving?

check_push_mule.prompt: Everybody push a mule that has decided not to move

onSuccess.narration: You heave, and the gem sack slips off the mule's back in the struggle. The moment it hits the ground, the mule leaps up, fresh as morning, and trots three steps away from it. "She'll carry anything," says the owner, amazed. "Anything but that, it seems."

onFailure.narration: You push. The mule leans. The mule wins, and you sit down in the road in a heap. From down there you notice the mule is not glaring at you at all. It is glaring at the gem sack on its own back. Its owner sees it too, and slowly takes the sack off.

scene_stubborn_mule_unload.narration: You lift off the gem sack. The mule springs up and steps away from it. "Anything but that, it seems," mutters the owner. You carry the sack to his wagon.

scene_stubborn_mule_ask_mule.narration: Your unicorn kneels by the mule. It is not stubborn. It is uneasy, the way you feel before a thunderstorm. And the feeling comes from the sack. The owner takes it off without a word.

rest_soup_tents.narration: By the road, helpers in dark robes serve soup in big tents. Little crystals hum on strings around their necks. A ladler named Wend waves you in. "Kindness first," says Wend.

variants.text: Beside the lane, people in dark robes have put up rest tents, with DEEP HOLLOW stitched small on the flaps. Behind the soup pot is Wend from the ford. "You made it across!" says Wend, and says each of your names without being told.

rest_soup_tents_rest_go.narration: You thank the helpers and fold your blankets. Wend waves the ladle, and a crystal bumps it and hums. Back to the road.

scene_wend_pitch.narration: "The world's a little broken, isn't it?" says Wend. "Wrong-colored sky, humming stones. We could fix it, right at the root. Will you carry a letter north for us?" Wend's crystal hums the stones' note. By the pot sits a coin box.

scene_wend_pitch_say_later.narration: "Maybe," you say. Wend nods as if maybe means yes, and slips a sealed letter into your pack, "in case." All day you feel it in there, like a stone in a boot.

scene_wend_pitch_say_no.narration: "No, thank you," you say, kindly and clearly. Wend smiles just as warmly, which is somehow the strangest part. "Kindness first anyway," says Wend, tucking a warm roll into your pack. The crystal keeps humming.

scene_wend_pitch_coin.narration: You drop a coin in the box. Its lid says FOR THE ROOT OF THINGS. Wend's crystal hums like a hive waking, and Wend writes your names in a little book. What did you just pay for?

scene_road_crew.narration: A centaur crew is moving the road around a scorched hollow, and the road boss wants help. Carry posts, and her crew will shelter you from tonight's ash wind. Or walk the detour with her and learn the way past the silly signs.

check_haul_posts.prompt: Everybody carry marker posts for a centaur road crew

onSuccess.narration: You carry posts until your arms feel like noodles, and you plant every one straight. The road boss looks down the new curve and nods. "Good work. The relay will sing about this," she says, and she does not sound like she is joking.

onFailure.narration: You carry a post backward and plant it upside down, so the arrow points at the sky. The crew decides this is very funny and leaves it there, as a joke for the next runner. The road boss thanks you anyway, still chuckling.

scene_road_crew_ask_why.narration: "Nothing will pass the hollow where the stone fell," says the road boss. She walks you along the detour: old bridge, pond, depot barn. Remember that order. It will get you past the silly signs ahead.

scene_road_crew_charm.narration: You hold the tuned charm over the hollow. It sings, faint and thin, though the stone was carried off weeks ago. The ground remembers. "Well," says the road boss. "That explains a thing or two."

scene_road_crew_fly.narration: From up high you see it. All along the north roads, little curves of new posts bend away from scorched hollows, like somebody stepping around puddles. The road is not wandering. It is stepping around something.

scene_warden_patrol.narration: A Skywarden patrol has stopped the road. Sergeant Holloway wants a toll of two coins, for Redspire, the wardens' citadel. "Only arithmetic," he says. He also has a form marked WORKS INSTEAD, with its own box.

scene_warden_patrol_griffin_logs.narration: Your griffin and the sergeant swap sky news like old flyers: wind at the bridge, ash over the mountain, a storm sitting on the sea. Holloway writes it all down. "Useful," he says, and waves you through.

scene_warden_patrol_pay.narration: You pay. Sergeant Holloway writes PAID, POLITE in his ledger and hands you a receipt, then a receipt for the receipt. "Arithmetic," he says, almost kindly. "The only thing up here that isn't shouting."

onSuccess.narration: You find a mistake in the sergeant's sums. Sergeant Holloway checks it twice, corrects it, and pays you back two coppers with deep respect.

onFailure.narration: Sergeant Holloway listens to your whole argument, writes it down in the ledger under 'Complaints, Polite', and charges you the fixed rate anyway.

scene_signposts.narration: Forty arrows promise GEMS THIS WAY. None of them agree. A man in a velvet coat sells guaranteed maps, refundable by his cousin, who has left. Three old relay notices name real landmarks.

check_read_signs.prompt: The best reader reads the signs and sorts the honest from the nonsense

onSuccess.narration: Most of the signs are nonsense. But a few old, weathered ones, nailed up by the relay, all agree about one thing: the road north bends away from every place a stone came down. You follow the honest arrows straight to the depot.

onFailure.narration: You follow the most convincing sign for half an hour and arrive at a pig farm. The pigs are friendly. The farmer points you back toward the depot, and politely waits until you are out of sight before he laughs.

scene_signposts_buy_map.narration: One coin buys a lovely drawing of a pig farm. A passing centaur points you to the real depot. The map remains a very good picture of pigs.

scene_signposts_outsell.narration: Your kitsune sets up next to him, selling honest maps that say ASK A CENTAUR. They sell out in ten minutes. The velvet-coated man buys one himself, then goes off to ask a centaur.

scene_depot.narration: Clerk Pennywhistle runs a depot barn full of strongboxes. Number nine rings like a dinner bell. That stone can be claimed, with the right paper. "There is a form for deciding which form," the clerk says happily.

check_forms.prompt: Fill in Form 9 with no smudges, in the right order

onSuccess.narration: Clerk Pennywhistle holds your form up to the lamp, finds no smudges, and looks as if he might cry with happiness. He stamps it four times.

onFailure.narration: You fill in Form 9. It needed Form 7B first. Clerk Pennywhistle is very sorry. The line behind you is not.

scene_strongbox.narration: Pennywhistle opens strongbox nine. "The Depot Stone. Claimed." He writes your names and hands over the ringing gem. "Keep it away from my pens." Behind him, strongbox ten gives a loud thump.

scene_depot_leave.narration: You leave the ringing stone in box nine. Pennywhistle relaxes and ticks UNCLAIMED. Behind him, another box gives a loud thump.

scene_rumor_fire.narration: At the noon stop, a ring of travelers is swapping news, and the news has clearly been swapped a great many times. "On the River Road," says one, "a troll charges you a story instead of a coin." "On the Wild Road," says another, "the marsh steals your boots and gives back different boots." Everybody turns to you. "What's your news?"

check_tall_tale.prompt: Tell a tall tale the whole ring believes

onSuccess.narration: You tell them you rode a river drake across the ford, sideways, wearing a hat. By the end the whole ring believes you, and three people are already retelling it with a bigger hat. By nightfall, the hat has feathers.

onFailure.narration: You start well, but you mix up the drake with the river, and the river with your aunt. The ring laughs kindly and decides your aunt must be a river. That rumor will be all over the Plains by Tuesday.

scene_rumor_fire_true_news.narration: Every gem hums the same note, you tell them. An old woman nods. "Noticed that," she says. A nearby wagon hums as if voting.

scene_rumor_fire_ford_news.narration: You tell them about the two-day line, the numbered pebbles, and Burdock's goat with a bucket on her head. By sunset the story has come back with three extra goats.

scene_rumor_fire_marsh_news.narration: You tell them the marsh does not steal boots. The boggarts only borrow things, keep careful records, and hum. One man takes off his boots and looks at them suspiciously.

scene_bell_courier.narration: A dragonling courier trots down from the north on a pony, ringing ding, ding, pause, ding. "Boundary news! It must reach the river," she pants. She looks very tired.

check_ring_pattern.prompt: Ring a bell pattern exactly right

onSuccess.narration: Ding, ding, pause, ding. You get it exactly right, and far away to the south, very faintly, another bell rings it back. The courier beams. "You'd make a grandmother one day," she says, which is the biggest compliment she knows.

onFailure.narration: Ding, pause, ding, ding, ding. The courier goes pink. "That one means the cake is ready," she whispers. Far to the south, a whole camp sits down hopefully to wait for cake. She takes the bell back, giggling, and rings it properly.

scene_bell_courier_ask_news.narration: "The grandmothers are turning back pry bars at the boundary stones," says the courier. "Whole wagons of them. Not spoons. Spoons are fine." Her pony nudges you for attention.

scene_bell_courier_ring_back.narration: You ring the answer every dragonling child knows: heard you, coming home. The courier's mouth falls open. "You're from the hills! The grandmothers will want YOU." She rings the news of you down the road, proud as anything.

scene_relay_sing.narration: At the relay campfire, centaurs sing one verse for each landmark. New detours mean new verses. "Your turn, travelers," hums a centaur called Old Corran. He wants your verse for the road.

check_sing.prompt: Sing a route-song verse in front of everybody

onSuccess.narration: Your voice wobbles once and then holds. The whole campfire sings the chorus back at you, and Old Corran thumps the ground with a hoof.

onFailure.narration: You sing the wrong verse, the one about a bridge three hundred miles away. Old Corran gently sings the right one over the top, and nobody minds at all.

scene_relay_sing_listen.narration: Old Corran sings slowly. Landmark after landmark, the road bends away from places where stones fell. Listen for the whole shape.

scene_relay_sing_crew_verse.narration: The road crew joins the fire. Their new verse is about travelers passing marker posts down a curve. It is about you! Old Corran makes the chorus rhyme with "noodles." Nobody asks how.

scene_spiral.narration: You hear the new verses in road order. They are not random. Every detour bends away from a place where stones fell. Sung end to end, the roads curl around the gemfalls like a snail shell. Old Corran scratches the verses onto bark for you.

scene_ash_wind.narration: Warm gray ash blows down from the mountain. Your packs hum louder. The ash is soft, but it gets everywhere, even up noses. How will you cross?

check_ash_wind.prompt: Link arms, lean into the ash wind and keep walking

onSuccess.narration: You link arms and march on through the glitter. It is like walking through warm gray snow. By the time the wind passes, you are gray from head to toe and look like a row of statues, and the bend in the road is just ahead.

onFailure.narration: The wind shoves you sideways into a hedge, one after another, like bowling pins. It is warm in the hedge, so you wait it out there, sneezing ash. When it passes you climb out, grayer and wiser, and the bend in the road is just ahead.

scene_ash_wind_shelter.narration: Sergeant Holloway is already behind the Skywarden supply wagon. "Third ash wind this week," he says, writing BUSY under MOUNTAIN. He offers you a cracker. It is extremely dry.

scene_ash_wind_fly_above.narration: Your griffin climbs above the ash into starlight. Below, the rush's lanterns curl north around dark patches, just like the verses. The road is singing the spiral with its feet.

scene_road_bend.narration: Cinder wolves pace across the bend ahead, glowing faintly. Plains folk say never camp at a bend. The wolves seem to agree. How will you get past?

check_sneak.prompt: Creep through the long grass without a rustle

onSuccess.narration: Not one blade of grass rustles. One wolf lifts its nose, sniffs, and goes back to pacing.

onFailure.narration: A jackalope pops out of the grass right in front of you, shouts its little jackalope shout, and every wolf turns your way.

encounter_wolves.narration: The wolves are cold and hungry and far from home. They would like this bit of road, please.

onVictory.narration: The pack backs off and trots north toward the hills, glowing like a string of lanterns.

onDefeat.narration: The pack bowls through your camp, and everyone scatters in the dark.

scene_road_bend_wait.narration: You wait. One by one, the wolves lift their noses toward the mountain and trot north. Waiting was a choice too.

end_foothills_in_sight.narration: You camp past the bend, safe. In the morning you see the red foothills, where the rush is heading. The bark of verses is in your pack. Now you know what the road is saying: the land is flinching from the stones.

variants.text: The crew you helped sheltered your wind crossing and took its screen onward. No borrowed screen remains in your packs.
The pig farmer fixed your route.
A relay runner helped with the signs.

end_scattered.narration: By the time you find your feet, it is almost morning. The wolves ate the supplies and ran north. Sergeant Holloway's patrol writes you down as 'Stragglers, Muddy'. You lost a day, but the bark of verses is safe, and so are you.

variants.text: The crew you helped sheltered your wind crossing and took its screen onward. No borrowed screen remains in your packs.
The pig farmer fixed your route.
A relay runner helped with the signs.

interaction_last_post.narration: The road boss holds a rope while you guide the last post into its hole. "The relay will find that in the dark," she says, and gives you a jar of glowing moss for the night.

interaction_gate.narration: Past the sergeant's table, a striped pole swings up and down. A patrol goat chews a ledger page. "Cross on the lift," says Holloway, writing GOAT, HUNGRY.

interaction.cue: Wait for the pole to swing up, then go!

onSuccess.narration: You slip under on the lift. The goat looks impressed.

onFailure.narration: The pole drops on your hat. Holloway writes DELAYED, POLITE. The goat eats your hat's feather.

onAssisted.narration: Holloway holds the pole up and writes ESCORTED, POLITE. The goat looks disappointed.

scene_box_ten.narration: Strongbox ten grows three legs and starts eating a ledger. Eleven tries to follow. "Mire mimics!" cries Pennywhistle. "Ten has been empty since spring!" Drive them out before they eat the stamps.

encounter_boxes.narration: The two boxes crash out into the yard, snapping their lids and burping ink. Drive them off before they swallow the paperwork!

scene_boxes_gone.narration: The mimics slink off, disguised as rocks. Pennywhistle thanks you with a brass whistle from lost property. "Lost since spring," he says. "So is my patience."

scene_boxes_sulking.narration: The boxes burp you out in a puff of ink. Pennywhistle slams a ledger on their lids, and the whole line sits on it until they shuffle off.

interaction_pony.narration: While the courier gulps water, her chubby pony nudges your elbow. Her name is Dumpling, and she is hot, itchy and sulky. "She wants a fuss," says the courier. "Any fuss will do."

interaction_verses.narration: Old Corran taps the new verses one landmark at a time, and each glows in the firelight. "Now tap them back in road order," he says.

interaction.cue: Watch the landmarks glow, then tap them back in the same order.

onSuccess.narration: You tap it back note for note. "There," says Old Corran. "The road just learned you."

onFailure.narration: You tap the pond twice, and the campfire giggles. Old Corran taps it right over yours, slow and kind.

onAssisted.narration: Old Corran taps the first landmark with you. "The road just learned you."

interaction_post_line.narration: The crew lines up along the new curve. Catch each post and pass it on. Alone, pass it to the road boss.

interaction.cue: Catch the marker post, then pass it along the curve.

onSuccess.narration: Every post lands right. "My crew will help if the ash wind catches you," says the road boss.

onFailure.narration: You plant a post upside down, arrow to the sky. The crew leaves it there as a joke.

onAssisted.narration: The road boss joins your line. Her crew will help if the ash wind catches you.

interaction_warden_tray.narration: You set Holloway's water tray beside the patrol cups, and a warden takes the far edge. The patrol goat drinks before Holloway can count. Still, the tray is level, and he stamps WORKED, POLITE. No coins needed.

interaction_relay_signs.narration: Forty signs promise GEMS THIS WAY. Three old relay notices give real landmarks. Share the clues, then put the landmarks in travel order.

interaction.cue: Share the clues. Choose the route landmarks in travel order.
clues: Cross the old bridge before reaching the pond.
The depot barn is after the pond.
The barn is the last landmark. Ignore the shiny GEM signs.

onSuccess.narration: Bridge, pond, barn: there's the depot!

onFailure.narration: You end up at a pig farm. The farmer reads the notices with you and points out which landmark comes first.

onAssisted.narration: A relay runner helps you compare. Bridge, pond, barn: there's the depot!

scene_signposts_checked.narration: Old bridge, pond, depot barn. You follow the road boss's detour, and the shiny GEM signs lose their argument.

scene_signposts_pigs.narration: The farmer draws bridge, pond, barn in the mud. A pig adds one hoofprint. "That bit is optional," says the farmer. Now you know the way to the depot.

interaction_form_nine.narration: Clerk Pennywhistle opens his claim book at STRONGBOX 9. Each hero says out loud why you want the stone, then makes a mark.

interaction.cue: Each hero says their claim aloud and adds a mark.

options.label: Write my name carefully
options.reaction: Pennywhistle gives the name a neat tick.

options.label: Leave a paw, hoof or handprint
options.reaction: Pennywhistle stamps beside the print. "Traditional," he says.

options.label: Ask the clerk to write for me
options.reaction: Pennywhistle reads the words back before adding a tick.

onSuccess.narration: The clerk reads your claim back and stamps it. Box nine is yours to open.

onFailure.narration: The clerk sets your claim aside. Behind him, a strongbox begins to jump.

onAssisted.narration: Pennywhistle helps write your words. Stamp! Box nine is yours.

interaction_courier_pattern.narration: The courier rings ding, ding, pause, ding. Watch, then echo it. "Don't skip the pause," she pants, "or people start looking for cake."

interaction.cue: Watch, then echo ding, ding, pause, ding.

onSuccess.narration: Ding, ding, pause, ding! Far south, another bell rings it back. The courier beams.

onFailure.narration: Ding, pause, ding, ding, ding. "That means the cake is ready," she whispers. Far south, a camp waits for cake.

onAssisted.narration: The courier points to each mark while you ring. The southern bell answers.

interaction_ash_load.narration: Link up around the shared load. Raise or lower your side until the marker sits in the middle, then walk. Ash piles up like gray snow.

interaction.cue: Raise or lower your side to level the shared load.

onSuccess.narration: You march through like a row of gray statues. The bend is just ahead.

onFailure.narration: The wind bowls you into a hedge. You wait it out, sneezing ash. Then on to the bend.

onAssisted.narration: A passing Skywarden braces the downwind end. You reach the bend gray with ash.

interaction_crew_screen.narration: The crew you helped parks its supply wagon across the wind. Hold the screen steady while the acting hero guides everyone through.

interaction.cue: Brace the wind screen while the acting hero guides the crossing.

onSuccess.narration: Everyone gets through. The crew packs up its screen and waves you on.

onFailure.narration: The screen flaps loose. The crew shelters everyone behind the wagon until the gust passes.

onAssisted.narration: The road boss anchors the screen with you, and everyone gets through.

interaction_pony_response_brush.narration: Dumpling leans into the brush and groans with joy. She blows a raspberry on your sleeve. The courier laughs and tips you three coppers. Off she rings, and you follow the sound of singing to the relay campfire.

interaction_pony_response_water.narration: Dumpling slurps until the bucket is just a shiny bottom. She blows a raspberry on your sleeve. The courier laughs and tips you three coppers. Off she rings, and you follow the sound of singing to the relay campfire.

interaction_pony_response_hum.narration: Dumpling's tail swishes in time. She blows a raspberry on your sleeve. The courier laughs and tips you three coppers. Off she rings, and you follow the sound of singing to the relay campfire.

voiceGuide.tone: road country in full flood; noisy, kind, a little melancholy on the downbound lane, a little spooky at night, never scary

npcVoices.drover: the lead drover from the ford; huge booming voice, calls the party 'mudlarks'
npcVoices.ma_ruddle: a sold-out prospector; tired, blunt, cares about Tib and nothing else
npcVoices.tib: a small boy in an orange hat; talks to horses, ponies and centaurs as equals
npcVoices.wend: a Deep Hollow ladler; gentle, generous, remembers every name, certain the world can be fixed at the root
npcVoices.sergeant_holloway: a Skywarden supply sergeant; rigid, honest, calls everything 'arithmetic', writes everything down
npcVoices.clerk_pennywhistle: a depot clerk; loves forms, horrified by smudges, very sorry about Form 7B
npcVoices.old_corran: an old centaur relay singer; slow, warm, sings more than he speaks
npcVoices.road_boss: a centaur road-crew boss; brisk and practical, a marker post on each shoulder, says 'a road goes where the walking goes'
npcVoices.map_seller: a map seller in a velvet coat; smooth, cheerful, never technically lies
npcVoices.rumor_ring: noon-stop travelers swapping news; eager, garbled, every story a little bigger each time

interaction_last_post.narration: At the end of the new curve lies the last marker post, the tall one, as heavy as a barn door. "One to steer, the rest to hold the ropes," says the road boss, tossing you a coil. "Straight up, mind. A crooked post sends the whole relay the wrong way."

interaction.cue: Friends hold the ropes tight while someone steers the post upright.

onSuccess.narration: The post goes up straight as a candle. The road boss stamps it in and grins. "The relay will find that in the dark," she says, and presses a jar of glowing moss into your hands for the night road.

onFailure.narration: The post wobbles, leans, and settles at a jaunty angle. The road boss tilts her head at it. "Adds character," she decides, and leaves it exactly there.

onAssisted.narration: The road boss takes a rope herself, and the post goes up straight as a candle. "The relay will find that in the dark," she says, and presses a jar of glowing moss into your hands for the night road.

interaction_warden_tray.narration: Holloway's water tray leans toward the road. Lift or lower your side until the marker is centered, then set it beside the patrol cups. "Every drop accounted for," the sergeant says. The goat has already claimed a cup.

interaction.cue: Raise or lower your side until the supply tray is level.

onSuccess.narration: The water tray settles level. Holloway stamps WORKED, POLITE. Your help pays for passage; no coins leave your purse.

onFailure.narration: Water slops over the side. Holloway steadies the tray, accepts the work, and waves you through without a coin charge.

onAssisted.narration: Holloway steadies a corner while you balance the tray. WORKED WITH HELP, POLITE goes in the ledger. Passage costs no coins.

interaction_pony.narration: While the courier gulps water, her fat pony nudges your elbow. Her name is Dumpling, and she is hot, itchy and sulky. "She wants a fuss," says the courier, with her mouth full. "Any fuss will do. She is not picky, except about carrots."

interaction.cue: Make a fuss of Dumpling until she stops sulking.

options.label: Brush her mane
options.reaction: Dumpling leans into the brush and groans with joy.

options.label: Pour her a bucket of water
options.reaction: Dumpling slurps until the bucket is just a shiny bottom.

onSuccess.narration: Dumpling blows a happy raspberry all over your sleeve. The courier laughs so hard she nearly drops the bell. "Nobody does that on the first try," she says, and tips three coppers into your hand. "Courier's tip. Do not tell the grandmothers." Then she is off down the road, ringing, and you follow the sound of singing to the relay campfire.
